Looking at the training examples, I need to understand the rule:

The grid is divided into cells by a separator color. Each cell is 2x2. When two cells of the same color appear in the same row or column, the cells between them (in that row/column) get filled with that color. Additionally, singleton colored cells that appear alone in their row/column seem to get extended vertically/horizontally to fill the gap between same-colored cells.

More precisely: For each color, if two instances appear in the same row of cells, fill all cells between them in that row with that color. If two instances appear in the same column of cells, fill all cells between them in that column with that color.

**Test 0:** Grid with separator 3, 2x2 cells. Colors 6, 9, 1 appear. Checking: 6 appears at (1,1) and (7,1) - same column, fill between. 1 appears at (5,5) and (5,7) - same row, fill between. Also 1 at (7,5) and (5,5)/(5,7) - column fills. The output follows this pattern correctly. ✓ **Consistent = 1**
